# Nuthatch

> A self-hosted, AI-native blockchain indexer in one Rust binary. A contract address becomes a
> live, queryable SQL API on your own machine, with no third-party data service in the path and
> nothing sent about you unless you say yes, once, to an anonymous head count. Tagline: "Be your own indexer."

Nuthatch turns an EVM contract's events into tables in a local database. Embedded mode is one
process with no external services: no Postgres, no Docker, no IPFS, no account. It is free and
licensed
MIT OR Apache-2.0. Status: v5.15.0, released 2026-10-31, on the stable 5.x line. 5.15.0 adds the embeddable engine (RFC-0077): nuthatch's core as a WebAssembly module (`nuthatch-events.wasm`, interface `abi: 1`), a separate opt-in artefact on the release for data that belongs to one user on one device; for a binary user nothing changes, and there is no storage migration. 5.14.1 corrects how a remote follower's visibility lag is measured, contains a panic while a nest joins a running runtime, and stops a refusing RPC endpoint from flooding the log. 5.14.0 scales the shared runtime (RFC-0076): a chain's SQL gate seats only tenants that are querying, `[runtime] sql_permits` sets its permits live, bounded by memory rather than 16; the nests on one chain progress independently behind one extraction stage, the default cursor for a runtime; and `nuthatch serve --follow` can serve from another host, reading the mirror and the registry. 5.13.0 is the shared runtime (RFC-0073): fair share between tenant labels, per-mount limits, the memory ceiling and chains changed live, fault containment, bundles and seeding over the admin API, per-nest metrics and a `Nuthatch-Cost` report, `POST /sql`, `nuthatch mcp --token-env`, counted undecoded logs, `[runtime] isolation = "strict"` (its guarantee not yet claimed) and read replicas. A lone nest behaves as before, and neither release migrates storage. 5.12.1 and 5.12.2 are security releases for operators who mount other people's nests. 5.12.0 widens what an address-history nest answers: off a loopback bind it answers `eth_blockNumber` from its own head and a watched account's balance, and an account with code keeps its token transfers on the chains proved by the balance. 5.11.1 makes a running publisher check each mirrored segment once, not on every pass. 5.11.0 is a cold audit of 5.10.0 put right and makes several behaviours stricter: the admin API needs a token on every bind (a localhost nest without `NUTHATCH_ADMIN_TOKEN` makes one in `<dir>/.admin-token`), `nuthatch control` refuses to start without `NUTHATCH_CONTROL_TOKEN`, a symlinked input file or a webhook that cannot work refuses the nest, and `/diff` refuses `top` above 1,000. 5.10.0 adds `nuthatch watch`, a read-only view of a running nest, and makes budgeted analytical reads read 2,048 rows at a time and treat addresses as 20-byte values inside a plan. 5.9.0 adds `nuthatch diff`: what
happened in a block range, a block or a transaction, in fixed sentences from the rows a nest already
holds; read-only, with no storage migration. 5.8.2 keeps a seal-direct backfill on a dense chain inside the memory budget. 5.8.1 refuses to reopen a store after an event's indexed parameters have moved. 5.8.0 fixes
the 107 defects of a cold audit of 5.7.2 and makes several defaults stricter: a set
`NUTHATCH_ADMIN_TOKEN` applies on localhost too, aliases and template names must match
`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, and `pack verify` needs `--pubkey`.

The 5.x line is a promise about upgrades, not a claim of completeness: from 5.0.0 to the last 5.x
release a config keeps working with the same meaning, a data directory opens in place on a later
release with no re-index or migration command, and no HTTP route, response field, generated table or
column, or MCP tool is removed, renamed or retyped. Downgrades, the off-by-default cargo features
(`graph`, `folds`, `counter`) and the SQL dialect behind `/sql` are not covered. 5.0.0 removed the
WASM transform layer and live screening: the `transform`, `screen` and `audit replay` subcommands
and the `screen_status` MCP tool are gone, and a `nuthatch.toml` with a `[screening]` table
is refused at load until the table is deleted.

This file is written for language models and coding agents. It separates what the released binary
does from what is designed and not built. The longer version is
https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/llms-full.txt. Every command below was run against the released
5.9.0 binary when this file was written.

## What it does today

- `nuthatch init <address>…` resolves each contract's ABI (Sourcify, then a keyless Blockscout,
  then Etherscan if `ETHERSCAN_API_KEY` is set; EIP-1967 and legacy proxies followed), detects the
  deployment block and scaffolds a nest: `nuthatch.toml`, vendored `abis/`, `schema.json`,
  `semantic.toml`, a commented `views/` starter, an `llms.txt` and a Claude Code skill. Omit
  `--chain` and it probes the nine built-in chains for the contract's bytecode. `--from <git-url |
  dir>` runs a published nest; `--from-subgraph <CID | url>` scaffolds from a subgraph manifest;
  `--abi <file>` is the escape hatch for a proxy whose implementation ABI no resolver returns.
- `nuthatch dev` is the serve command. It backfills, follows the tip, decodes every declared event
  of every contract into a table named `{alias}__{event}` (an empty typed table even before the
  event has fired), keeps the reorgable tip in an embedded redb store, seals finalised ranges to
  content-addressed Parquet, and serves an HTTP API on `127.0.0.1:8288`. Every row carries
  `block_number`, `block_hash`, `block_timestamp`, `tx_hash`, `log_index`, `address` and `_seq`;
  every integer wider than 64 bits is an exact decimal string with a `{col}_dec` DECIMAL sibling
  and a `{col}_overflow` flag.
- Analytical SQL over the live tip and the sealed history as one surface, through `GET /sql`,
  `nuthatch sql` and the MCP `sql` tool. The engine is Burrmill, an embedded query engine on Apache
  DataFusion, since 4.1.0 (2026-10-02). Releases up to 4.0.2 used DuckDB, which is no longer in the
  binary; the sealed segments are plain Parquet and DuckDB or Trino can still read them.
- Built-in derived state: balances maintained incrementally (DBSP) from transfers, served at
  `/balances` and `/balance/{address}`; a reorg is a retraction. `nuthatch recipe add
  total_supply|balances|holder_count|reserves` derives what a subgraph pays an archive node to
  `eth_call` for, as an ordinary SQL view. `nuthatch metadata fetch` reads `decimals`, `symbol` and
  `name` once and caches them.
- Authored logic: `views/*.sql` are `CREATE VIEW` statements evaluated when a reader asks, bound
  against the schema at load so a moved column fails `nuthatch check` loudly. `entities.toml`
  declares an authored incremental entity (stable since 3.0.0): one `SELECT`, a unique key and
  `max_rows`, maintained as blocks arrive, retracted on reorg, served by name on `/sql` and at
  `/derived/{entity}`. On the Lodestar nest the view it replaced went from 2.15 s to 87.7 ms. A nest
  declaring an entity cannot run with `dev --seal-direct`; the refusal is deliberate.
- Pinned contract reads and verified documents: a `[[calls]]` block samples an `eth_call` at fixed
  blocks (or one call per row of a table), needing `--state-rpc` against an archive node; an
  `[[ipfs]]` block resolves a CID named in a column and refuses any body that does not hash to it.
- Factories: `[[templates]]` and `[[factories]]` index the children a contract deploys at runtime,
  sharing one table per template, distinguished by `address`. It indexes Uniswap. Since 4.11.0 it
  asks for logs by factory and child addresses until 500 children, then by topic0; since 5.13.0 a solo
  nest's tip fetch and a seal-direct backfill keep static contracts on addresses and flip only
  templates with children. An endpoint
  that caps the addresses in one `eth_getLogs` has the list halved rather than read as a credentials
  refusal.
- The compliance pack (opt-in): content-addressed label and list snapshots, threshold and velocity
  flags at `/flags`, counterparty exposure at `/exposure/{address}`, alert and row webhooks over a
  durable at-least-once outbox, a signed pack manifest, and `audit report` over the threshold flags.
- A built-in MCP server (`nuthatch mcp`, stdio, bridging to a running `dev`): 12 tools in all, of
  which eight (`status`, `schema`, `tables`, `table`, `sql`, `explain`, `entity`, `diff`) are
  advertised on every nest, `balance` and `top_balances` where the nest decodes transfers, and `flags` and
  `exposure` where compliance is configured; three resources
  (`nuthatch://schema|tables|status`); three prompts (`profile-contract`, `verify-a-number`, and
  `investigate-address` where compliance is configured). A token nest therefore advertises ten
  tools and two prompts. Results carry a provenance stamp (`as_of`, `sealed_through`, `nid`,
  `registry_hash`). `GET /explain` validates a query without running it.
- Nests as packages: `nuthatch nest bundle` writes a content-addressed `.bundle`; `nest load`
  verifies every file's hash and regenerates the decode registry before installing; `nest publish`
  and `nest load name@version --registry <dir | s3://bucket/prefix>` share them by name and by
  NID. `nuthatch nest nid` prints the identity a nest's data lives under (`data/<nid>/`).
- One runtime, many nests: `nuthatch dev --dir <dir>` runs one nest over a `nuthatch.toml` or many
  over a `mounts.toml`, with one isolated cursor per chain, nests on a chain sharing its cursor, a
  per-cursor RAM ceiling, and a nest that faults quarantined rather than fatal. There is no
  `roost` subcommand; it was removed in 2.0. A runtime may start empty and be driven over the admin
  API: `POST /_admin/nests {name, nid}` mounts a NID as a job, fetching it from `--registry`;
  `?dry_run=true` prices it; suspend, resume, move to a new NID with no gap, and unmount with
  `?reclaim=true` are routes too. A tenant is an opaque label in a mount name (`acme/usdc`); two
  mounts of one NID share one dataset and it is never indexed twice. Since 5.13.0 an operator can
  set each label's share of a chain's SQL permits (`PUT /_admin/tenants/<tenant>`), lower a mount's
  query limits, change the memory ceiling, SQL permits and chains live, seed a mount from a mirror,
  and run read replicas with `nuthatch serve --follow <writer>`; nuthatch still authenticates and
  bills no one.
- The mirror: `nuthatch publish sync --target <dir | s3://bucket/prefix>` mirrors sealed segments
  and the catalogue, `dev --publish-target` does it as they seal, `publish verify` and `publish
  status` check it, and `publish finalise` (4.8.0) marks a stopped nest's provisional tails final.
  `nuthatch seed --from <mirror> --dir <nest>` (4.9.0) fills a nest that has not indexed from such a
  mirror, checking every file against its hash, and the next `dev` follows the chain from where the
  mirror ends. A public mirror of nine datasets (Graph Protocol nests, defi-pulse-nest and the retired
  BetSwirl stopgap) is at https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/mirror.
- Sealed-history audit (4.5.0): `nuthatch audit sealed --rpc <second endpoint>` re-fetches a sample
  of sealed ranges and compares them row by row; `dev --audit-rpc` does it in the background.
- `[extract] l1_blocks = true` (4.6.0) adds an `l1_blocks` table on a chain that reports its L1
  block in every header (Arbitrum); a header without the field refuses the window rather than
  storing a zero. Turning it on for a nest that has already indexed is refused.
- Scaled mode (opt-in at build time, the `-scaled` artifacts): a control plane, a writer pool
  taking one lease per chain cursor with the fence enforced by the store, and an independently
  scaled query tier. Verified across real machines, including 377 blocks indexed through a
  90-second control-plane outage.
- Chains built in: Ethereum mainnet, Arbitrum One, Base, BSC, Polygon, Gnosis, Optimism, Monad and
  Robinhood Chain, each with keyless public endpoints and a finality policy. Any other EVM chain
  works with `--chain <name> --rpc <url>`; it inherits depth-64 finality and a 20-block `getLogs`
  window, and its `chain_id` is verified against every endpoint at startup. The bundled public
  endpoints are for trying it out; they are rate-limited, sometimes answer empty instead of
  erroring, and are not for production.
- Maintained views (4.14.0): a view listed in `maintained.toml` is answered from a stored copy of
  its own evaluation, keyed on every input it read, and used only when those inputs hash the same, so
  a copy is never stale. A nest that declares none behaves as before.
- Address history (5.1.0 to 5.7.0): a `nuthatch.toml` with an `[address_history]` table and no
  `[[contracts]]` watches accounts and serves their history at `GET /api` in Etherscan's shapes, for
  rotki (https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/rotki). Answers are exact or refused. Ethereum, Optimism,
  Base, Arbitrum, Polygon, BNB Chain and Gnosis; several chains behind one `dev --dir`. The deposit
  sweep (`[address_history.sweep]`, 5.4.0) reads each block once for a whole watched set. `nuthatch
  partitions` builds verified block partitions a nest can start from; the Ethereum ones are published
  (https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/nests/hosted/ethereum-address-history).
- `nuthatch diff` (5.9.0), with `GET /diff` and the MCP `diff` tool: what happened in a block range,
  a block or a transaction, in fixed sentences with exact amounts from the rows a nest already holds.
  No model, nothing inferred.
- In a browser (https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/play): Burrmill compiled to WebAssembly answers SQL
  over a published nest's hash-checked segments in the tab; the nest builder scaffolds and indexes a
  nest from a contract address there; a postcard is a `/play` link pinned to a nest's segments by
  hash. None of it changes the binary.

## Guards and limits

`/sql` accepts one `SELECT` or `WITH` statement per request, at most 16 KiB of text, and refuses
file-reading functions by denylist and by an allowlist over the engine's own parse. Defaults: a 30 s
timeout (answered 504), a 50,000-row cap, a 64 MiB result ceiling, two concurrent statements (a
third waits 250 ms, then 503), two million unsealed tip rows per query (refused with 503 rather than
answered from sealed data alone). The engine runs each session under a memory limit
(`NUTHATCH_ANALYTICS_MEMORY_LIMIT`, 512 MB by default) and a thread cap, and since 4.4.0 every
session over one nest draws on one pool (`NUTHATCH_BURRMILL_MEMORY_LIMIT`); a statement that needs
more is refused, not spilled. 4.10.0 added `NUTHATCH_RUNTIME_HEADROOM` and a lower
`NUTHATCH_INGESTION_RESERVATION`, and the startup check refuses a configuration that does not fit
the cursor's budget, naming the largest value that would. A repeated statement is answered from a
cache (`"cached": true`) keyed since 4.11.0 on the rows and segments it reads. The API has no authentication of its own:
bind localhost (the default) and put a proxy in front, or set `sql = "allowlist"` on a mount so
callers get named queries at `/q/{name}` and never send SQL.

## Footprint and speed, measured

- Budget: at most 2 GB RAM per active-chain cursor, enforced rather than aspired to. CI fails a
  build whose peak RSS passes 256 MB indexing a fixed 8,004-row fixture. The release gate serves a
  copy of the largest nest we run, the Lodestar allocations nest, under its production limits and
  runs the 74 statements its consumers send, two at a time; a peak over 2 GiB fails it. 4.4.0 peaked
  at 1,595 to 1,788 MiB over four runs. 4.10.0 took a copy of the QoS nest, two statements at a
  time, from 1,746 to 1,749 MiB down to 1,298 to 1,349 MiB with identical answers.
- Sentio's OBIB benchmark, case 6 (the Uniswap V2 factory over 10,001 mainnet blocks, 232 pairs
  discovered as it ran): 4.67 s median of five runs of the published 4.7.0 binary against a keyless
  public gateway, 35,271 events in 14 RPC requests at 229 MB peak RSS
  (https://github.com/nuthatch-org/nuthatch/blob/main/docs/bench/obib-case6-4.7.0-tenderly-2026-10-05.md). The event count matches
  Sentio's; the stopwatch is one workload under one set of conditions.
- No seal-direct or pipeline multiplier is quoted. The 8.7x and 20x figures were withdrawn in
  2.7.0 when their baseline was traced to an obsolete harness.
- Running a nest at tip costs RPC requests. Since 4.15.2 a nest with no `--poll-interval` polls every
  five minutes. Following every block cost about 9,900 CU a minute, roughly $185 a month, against a
  paid Arbitrum endpoint (2026-09-06); five-minute polling is about a hundred times less for the
  same rows.

## Not built (design targets)

reth ExEx tip ingestion against a colocated node (the Source trait is in; the ExEx is designed, not
built, and wiring it needs a synced node) and firehose-class extraction on top of it; streaming subscribe (SSE); local models
(Ollama) or bring-your-own-key; wildcard signature-scoped indexing; a Homebrew tap. GraphQL (RFC-0053) shipped in 3.7.0 as a
partial read surface, exact for a subgraph's event-shaped fields and a named refusal for the rest;
it is parked, and only the `nuthatch-graph-<target>` download attached to every release since
4.11.0 serves it. The default binary and the images answer those routes with 404. Do not describe
it as a drop-in subgraph replacement.

Nuthatch publicly offers to host nests on request (https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/subgraphs): the
stock binary run as an operator would, no billing, no accounts; ask on Discord. The subgraph stopgap
nests it served from 2026-10-06 were withdrawn on 2026-10-13
(https://learn-thegraph.com/dispatches/stopgap-nests-for-stranded-subgraphs/; the first handback is
https://github.com/nuthatch-org/nuthatch/blob/main/docs/stopgap/betswirl-bnb.md).

## Install and first run

```sh
curl -fsSL https://nuthatch-indexer.com/install.sh | sh
nuthatch --version
nuthatch init 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 --alias weth --chain mainnet
nuthatch dev --backfill 300
nuthatch sql 'SELECT dst, wad FROM weth__transfer ORDER BY block_number DESC LIMIT 5'
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8288/sql?q=SELECT+count(*)+FROM+weth__transfer'
nuthatch mcp --print-config
```

`--backfill 300` starts 300 blocks behind the tip so there are rows within seconds; without it
`dev` backfills from the deployment block, which for a long-lived contract wants your own
archive-capable RPC. WETH names its transfer fields `src`, `dst` and `wad`; most ERC-20s use
`from`, `to` and `value`, and `from` must be double-quoted in SQL. `nuthatch recipe add
total_supply` on this WETH nest fails `nuthatch check` with `no column from` until the view's
columns are renamed, as the docs say. Prebuilt binaries cover macOS Apple Silicon, Linux x86_64
and, from 4.12.0, Linux arm64 (glibc 2.35 or newer from 4.1.0; no C++ runtime), each with a
`nuthatch-graph-<target>` sibling that serves GraphQL; `cargo +1.95.0 install --git
https://github.com/nuthatch-org/nuthatch nuthatch` builds elsewhere, and the toolchain pin is
required because `rust-toolchain.toml` does not apply to `cargo install`. Images:
`ghcr.io/nuthatch-org/nuthatch:5.9.0` and `:5.9.0-scaled`, `linux/amd64` only. Every artifact
has a `.sha256` and a GitHub build-provenance attestation (`gh attestation verify <tarball> --repo
nuthatch-org/nuthatch`).

Upgrading the binary is a swap and a restart. Two old patches matter if you advise on a version:
v0.9.3 fixed an arbitrary file read through `/sql` (DuckDB, the engine then, accepted a quoted
function name the guard did not match) and v0.6.2 fixed an arbitrary file write through
`;`-stacked statements. Both are on the repository's Security tab.

## Documentation

- [Quickstart](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/start/quickstart/): address to live API in under two minutes.
- [Install](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/start/install/): installer, images, source build, attestation.
- [What is a nest?](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/concepts/nests/): a content-addressed spec, not a program.
- [Runtimes and cursors](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/concepts/runtimes/): one cursor per chain, the single-cursor law.
- [Storage and sealing](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/concepts/storage/): redb tip, Parquet past finality, one SQL surface.
- [Reorgs and finality](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/concepts/reorgs/): reorgs touch only the hot store.
- [Determinism](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/concepts/determinism/): LLM output never sits in the data path.
- [Nest identity and reuse](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/concepts/nest-identity/): NID, data identity, dataset adoption.
- [nuthatch.toml](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/build/config/) and the [configuration reference](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/reference/config/).
- [ABIs, events and tables](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/build/tables/): the column mapping and big integers.
- [Authored SQL views](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/build/views/) and [incremental entities](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/build/entities/).
- [Factories](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/build/factories/), [recipes](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/build/recipes/), [contract calls and IPFS](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/build/contract-calls/).
- [Compliance pack](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/build/compliance/) and [webhooks](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/build/webhooks/).
- [Build a subgraph fallback](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/build/subgraph-fallback/): the boundary of event-derived data.
- [CLI guide](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/reference/cli/); the generated full reference is `skills/nuthatch-builder/cli-reference.md` in the repository.
- [HTTP API](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/reference/http-api/), [the SQL surface](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/reference/sql/), [MCP server](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/reference/mcp/).
- [Run it in production](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/operate/production/), [deploy](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/operate/deploy/), [security](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/operate/security/).
- [Metrics and footprint](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/operate/metrics/), [performance](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/operate/performance/), [what it costs](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/operate/costs/).
- [Run many nests](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/operate/many-nests/), [host nests for others](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/operate/hosting-nests/), [the registry](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/operate/registry/).
- [Upgrading a nest](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/operate/upgrades/), [verifying a deployment](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/operate/verifying/), [troubleshooting](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/operate/troubleshooting/).
- [Scaled mode](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/operate/scaled/): the fleet.
- [Agent-grade MCP](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/ai/mcp/), [llms.txt in a nest](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/ai/llms-txt/), [the builder skill](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/ai/builder-skill/).
- [The book](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/book/): why the machine is shaped as it is, read against 5.9.0.
- [Architecture](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/contributing/architecture/) and [RFCs](https://www.nuthatch-indexer.com/docs/contributing/rfcs/).
